newsitem.title: USA: CBOT soy products close lower on stocks estimate.
newsitem.headline: CBOT soy products close lower on stocks estimate.

text.p: CBOT soy product futures ended lower after USDA surprised the market by leaving the 1996-97 soybean ending stocks estimate unchanged at 140 million bushels, traders said.
Traders had anticipated USDA would shave 10 million to 15 million bushels off the ending stocks estimate, leaving the figure closer to 130 million bushels.

USDA said crushing rates would increase by 10 million bushels but soymeal ending stocks were kept unchanged at 200,000 tons. Soyoil stocks were lowered to 1.9 billion lbs from 1.965 billion in February's report.
The market was also hit by news USDA expected soybean exports to drop by a record level in the last half of this marketing year, possibly below 900 million bushels.
But soymeal traded higher several times during the session, confirming a bullish trend, floor sources said.
"It acts pretty good. It wasn't much of a break at all and I think it was encouraging for the bulls," said Vic Lespinasse of Dean Witter.
Soymeal ended $4.90 to $1.00 per ton lower with May off $1.90 at $273.80. Soyoil closed 0.27 to 0.16 cent per lb lower with May off 0.16 at 26.17 cents.
Traders also cited news Brazil's soybean exports will likely increase by 74 percent over 1996 figures, according to consulting group Safras e Mercado.
Safras estimated exports at 6.3 million tonnes, well above their December projection for 5.8 million tonnes.
The projected sharp increase is due to the lifting of a state export tax last year which should favor soybean exports over soymeal and soyoil, Safras said.
The consultants also said soymeal imports were expected to rise 34 percent to 150,000 tonnes while soyoil purchases were forecast to jump 36 percent to 200,000 tonnes.
On the day, Cargill Inc bought 800 lots May soymeal, Iowa Grain and Rosenthal Collins each bought 400 lots May and Tenco Inc bought 200 lots each March and May and sold 150 May.
In soyoil, Cargill Inc bought 600 lots May and sold 500 May. ADM sold 800 July and 200 May and Produce Grain bought 500 May and sold 250 May.
Prudential Securities bought 400 May and 300 July, Tenco Inc bought 400 May and Smith Barney bought and sold 300 May.
Soymeal volume was estimated by CBOT at 26,000 lots, against Monday's actual volume of 33,141 lots. Soyoil volume was pegged at 31,000 lots, compared with Monday's 41,799.
